items.title: 中共五中全會閉幕：出席委員較本屆初減少四分之一 張升民罕見增選入政治局
items.description: 專家稱，更好的激勵與監督可能減少浪費、提高政策可預期性，但更嚴厲的紀律約束也可能加深幹部不敢作為的局面，拖延支出和投資。
items.content:
中共五中全會閉幕：出席委員較本屆初減少四分之一 張升民罕見增選入政治局
中共第二十屆中央委員會第五次全體會議（五中全會）周四（10月29日）在北京閉幕。官方發布的會議公報顯示，全會通過《中共中央關於持之以恆推進全面從嚴治黨若干重大問題的決定》，並增選中央軍委副主席張升民為中央政治局委員。
本次全會共有162名中央委員和117名候補中央委員出席，合計279人，較去年四中全會減少36人。二十大於2022年選出205名中央委員和171名候補中央委員，合計376人，本次出席人數約為其74%。
全會同時確認中央政治局此前對33名黨政及軍方高層作出的開除黨籍處分，包括馬興瑞、張又俠、劉振立、藍天立和劉建超等人，並確認給予李雲澤撤銷黨內職務處分。
會議還決定，中共第二十一次全國代表大會將於2027年下半年在北京召開。在高層換屆前一年，全會除了處理人事與紀律問題，也對幹部選任、黨內監督及反腐工作作出部署。
張升民入政治局，32年再屆中增選
68歲的張升民長期在軍隊政治工作和紀檢監察系統任職，曾任中央軍委紀律檢查委員會書記。去年10月，二十屆四中全會增補他為中央軍委副主席，此次再獲增選為中央政治局委員。
新華社在全會閉幕後公布的簡歷顯示，張升民生於1958年8月，陝西武功人，1978年入伍，現為火箭軍上將，並兼任中央紀委副書記。
他的晉升與軍方高層接連受到紀律處分同時發生。2022年二十屆一中全會確定的中央軍委領導班子共有7人，去年四中全會確認對何衛東、苗華等人的開除黨籍處分，今年五中全會又確認對張又俠、劉振立等人的處分。在這7人中，目前仍在任的只有軍委主席習近平和副主席張升民。公報沒有宣布增補其他軍委成員。
在中央委員會任期中途增選政治局委員，中共歷史上有先例，但近年罕見。上一次是1994年9月，十四屆四中全會增選時任上海市長黃菊為政治局委員，他隨後接任上海市委書記。張升民此次獲增選，時隔32年。更早的1985年，十二屆五中全會曾一次增選田紀雲、喬石、李鵬等6人進入政治局。2004年徐才厚雖在全會上升任中央軍委副主席，但直到2007年換屆時才進入政治局。
出席人數減少，34人處分獲確認
值得關注的是，根據新華社消息，共有162名中央委員和117名候補中央委員出席此次全會，合計279人。相較於2025年四中全會的168名中央委員及147名候補中央委員，共減少36人。
2022 年召開二十大時，中央委員會共205人、候補委員共171人，共 376人。之後歷次全會則會處理部分中央委員，遞補部分候補委員為新任中央委員，直至五中全會一共有279人出席，本次出席人數約占本屆初的74%，換言之，比最初名額少了超過四分之一。
在紀律處分方面，全會審議通過中央紀委有關18人的審查報告，以及中央軍委有關16人的審查報告，合計涉及34人。其中33人被開除黨籍，李雲澤被撤銷黨內職務。
公報明確指出，這些是中央政治局此前已作出的處分，全會此次予以確認，並不代表上述人員均在會議期間首次被查。
中央紀委國家監委10月27日通報，今年1月至9月，全國紀檢監察機關共立案80萬件，其中對73名省部級及以上幹部立案。同期共有68萬人受到處分，包括105名省部級及以上幹部。
長期研究中國政治與反腐運動的美國喬治亞州立大學政治學教授安德魯·魏德曼（Andrew Wedeman）此前在接受BBC中文訪問時指出：「習近平發起的反腐整肅運動至今已持續逾十年，不僅沒有停止，近年來反而進一步加劇。」
從嚴治黨與「不敢作為」
全面從嚴治黨是本次全會的主題。公報提出保持懲治腐敗高壓態勢，同時部署幹部管理、組織建設、黨內法規、監督體系及管黨治黨責任，內容並不只涉及案件查處。
其中一項突出的政治表述，是公報專段闡釋「習近平黨建思想」，將其定位為習近平新時代中國特色社會主義思想的重要組成部分，並要求深入學習貫徹。
這一提法並非首次出現，今年6月的全國黨建工作座談會已對學習貫徹作出部署，五中全會則將其納入全會公報的整體要求。
對領導幹部如何行使權力，公報要求嚴格執行領導班子決策議事規則，規範「一把手」履職用權，並提出增強制度執行力、「大力破除潛規則」。這些要求也與換屆安排相連。公報提出，結合換屆，對新任職領導班子成員特別是「一把手」開展政績觀培訓，要求他們「為人民出政績、以實幹出政績」。
亞洲協會政策研究所中國分析中心在會前發表的文章指出，從嚴治黨面對的一個核心問題，是如何讓各級官員既服從中央要求，又能有效施政。
該文認為，更好的激勵與監督可能減少浪費、提高政策可預期性，但更嚴厲的紀律約束也可能加深幹部不敢作為的局面，拖延支出和投資。文章提出，值得觀察的是《決定》能否讓幹部明確工作優先次序，並為合理探索提供可信的保障，而不只是增加問責依據。

items.title: 香港宏福苑大火報告公開：特首率官員鞠躬道歉，房屋局長請辭
items.description: 這場造成168人死亡的大火發生將近一年後，香港特首李家超首次率領官員鞠躬道歉。
items.content:
香港宏福苑大火報告公開：特首率官員鞠躬道歉，房屋局長請辭
在歷經四個月的聆訊調查後，中國香港特區政府公開大埔宏福苑大火獨立委員會調查報告。這場發生於2025年11月底的大火合共造成168人死亡，包括一名消防員殉職。
特區行政長官李家超週四（10月29日）率領多名官員召開記者會，他與一眾出席官員首次就事件鞠躬致歉，又指「政治任命團隊會承擔政治責任」，房屋局長何永賢週三（28日）已請辭。
週四公開的這份報告分成兩冊，共16個章節，逾1,000頁，部份內容因與刑事審判內容相關遭遮蓋。報告稱大火「極有可能」由一根香煙引起，而竹棚上的非阻燃棚網、窗戶上的發泡膠板等，讓火勢迅速蔓延。
記者會上，李家超多次被問及為何只有一名官員須負政治責任，他僅強調決定綜合考慮多個因素；一位宏福苑居民對BBC中文評論說，道歉來得太遲。
大火如何發生？
位於新界東北的大埔宏福苑於1983年落成，一共八座、每座31層，合共近2000個單位、4000多名居民，是英國管治時期政府建設的出售型「居者置其屋」公共房屋。
屋苑八座樓宇，從東至西，順序為宏志閣、宏盛閣、宏昌閣、宏泰閣、宏建閣、宏新閣、宏道閣和宏仁閣。
自2024年開始，宏福苑展開大型翻新工程，造價高達3.36億港元（4,282萬美元；2.89億元人民幣；14.09億元新台幣）。工程期間，屋苑全被竹棚和綠色棚網包裹。
2025年11月26日下午，火勢先從宏昌閣一樓位置竄起，短短一個小時內蔓延至屋苑八座大廈中的七座，入夜升至香港火警分級制度中的第五級——僅次於最嚴重的「災難級」。
委員會在報告中提出的起火時間為「14:30至14:40之間」，消防處在14:51接獲報警。大火最後焚燒43個小時，共造成168人死亡，包括一名消防員殉職。
獨立委員會報告稱，根據證據，火災「極有可能」是有熱源點燃紙質物料，而這熱源「很可能是一根香煙」。
委員會認定導致這場火災以及其重大傷亡的人為過失、錯誤或疏忽的因素還包括：
- 工人在工地的行為，例如吸煙及任由垃圾在如平台及竹棚工作台堆積
- 使用不安全的建築物料，例如非阻燃棚網及帆布、發泡膠板
- 採用不安全的建築工序
- 不合資格人士不當操作消防裝置
報告點名宏福苑維修工程的總承建商宏業公司及工程顧問鴻毅公司，宏業管理者侯華建及何建業，鴻毅管理者黃俠然，鴻毅時任董事兼註冊檢驗人員吳躍，是大火的「罪魁禍首」，「須為造成這場火災和嚴重傷亡負責」。
此次火警是香港17年來首宗五級大火，也是1997年主權移交以來第二宗。
報告寫道，「最遺憾的是」，一系列的安全隱患與風險，「釀成香港史上其中一宗最具毀滅性的火災」。
僅一名官員落馬
李家超週四在記者會開始之際表示，對宏福苑火災深感難過，「代表特局政府向災民及廣大巿民表示道歉」，並率領一眾官員鞠躬。
他隨即表示「政治任命團隊會承擔政治責任」，雖不涉個人犯錯，房屋局局長何永賢應承擔政治責任，又指她週三已請辭，週四起停止職務， 並將由副財政司長黃偉綸兼任署理房屋局長；李家超已報請中國中央政府免除何永賢的職務。
特區政府在公佈何永賢辭職後發佈她的書面聲明，當中稱她願意為宏福苑火災承擔政治責任，「希望逝者可以安息，家人可以安心前行，早日走出傷痛」。
李家超在記者會上多次被問及，何永賢任期只剩幾個月，只有一名官員落馬，問責力度是否足夠；被報告點名的部門首長是否有同樣政治責任。
李家超僅強調問責決定綜合考慮多方面因素，包括官員的角色、其政策範圍和事件的關係、問題屬性是政策問題還是執行問題、下屬的行事表現及政治團隊未來需要處理的大量工作等，甚至一度回應稱「不如給多些時間回答其他問題。」
至於被問到他本人是否在問責範圍之內，李則指，考慮政府要推行大量改革，其責任在「帶領政府解決問題」、落實工作。
會上亦問及，大火已發生接近一年，道歉會否太遲。李家超表示，火災後即時首要任務是拘捕疑犯，同時要援助和安置受影響的家庭，「到了現在這個階段」，認為是「適當的時候」代表政府道歉。
行政問責：啟動公務員調查
李家超在記者會提及除了政治問責外，亦會就行政及刑事方面問責。
政府將啟動「部門首長責任制」兩級調查機制，轉介公務員敍用委員會，李家超要求在3個月內完成調查，並指「最低級到最高級、即部門首長也是調查對象」。
委員會估計會與約100名公務員會面，當中40至50人是受查對象。由於房屋局局長何永賢屬政治委任官員而非公務員，不屬「部門首長責任制」的調查範圍。
將領導調查的公務員敍用委員會主席鄭美施指出，小組會以獨立委員會報告及早前公開的大量資料為起點，調查相關部門的個別公務員履行職務時有否缺失、違反公務員守則或規定等。
「部門首長責任制」由李家超在2025年《施政報告》中提出，機制分兩級，一般性質的調查由部門首長負責；嚴重、系統性或涉及首長的問題則啟動第二級調查，由公務員敍用委員會負責。
機制設有五級紀律處分：譴責、嚴厲譴責、罰款、降級、迫令退休、革職。
港澳辦：「實事求是、責罰相適」
被問及決定有否向北京查詢意見、或當局有否「硬指示」；以及為何由何永賢自行請辭而非免職，李家超稱處理宏福苑的後續工作，作為行政長官是「第一責任人」及「香港的當家人」，由他作出決定全面考慮。
隨後，中國國務院港澳事務辦公室以筆名「港澳平」發表題為《嚴肅問責勇擔當，聚力改革向前行》的評論文章，表示特區政府道歉，並循三方面問責、追責，是「實事求是、責罰相適」；又形容充分體現特區政府作為「當家人」和第一責任人的責任擔當。中聯辦發言人亦發表類似說法。
港澳辦的文章另指，在宏福苑火災善後過程中，「一些別有用心的人歪曲事故真相，借災難製造社會對立、煽動對政府的不滿，妄圖『以災亂港』」，認為對「反中亂港」的言行必須保持高度警惕，堅決打擊。
政府將如何改革？
除問責外，政府針對報告的發現及建議宣布多項改革措施。
李家超引述委員會報告稱，政府四個監督部門有不足及缺失，包括：房屋署旗下的獨立審查組、屋宇署、消防署和勞工處；維修因涉及巨額金錢，容易成為黑社會以及違法分子非法謀財的對象，以恐嚇、欺詐和腐敗手段圍標壟斷。
報告亦指出，有人涉嫌使用非阻燃棚網、發泡膠及其他易燃物料，為求工程方便擅自在走火樓梯開設生口等導致火勢迅速蔓延和大量傷亡；又指沿用多年的監管制度倚賴註冊承辦商及專業人士，但已「命存實亡」。
就此，李家超強調「問題的開端是圍標」，故須立法禁止樓宇維修工程圍標；另會成立跨部門特遣隊，成員將來自警方、廉政公署和競爭事務委員會，主動聯合調查相關個案，並成立樓宇維修支援及服務局，為巿民提供獨立的支援服務。
當局擬修訂三條法例，將樓宇大型維修工程的圍標行為刑事化，一經定罪最高可判監禁10年及罰款1,000萬港元。
另外針對樓宇維修工程長期存在的流弊，政府計劃於今年底前向立法會提交《建築物條例》修訂建議，改變過往依賴業界自律的模式，由政府主動加強工程審批、巡查和監管，並大幅提升違規行為的罰款上限。
政務司司長會領導督導委員會，檢視或落實獨立委員會提出的各項建議。
居民怎麼看？
宏福苑宏盛閣居民梁浩軒向BBC中文表示，特首及官員是「好事」，「但太遲了」，認為可更早公開道歉及慰問；又指政府毋須等待獨立委員會報告已可啟動針對公務員的調查。
就政府提出各項改革施，他表示，過去政府也曾提出杜絕圍標，但奈何「要監管的人不監管；要有責任的人不承擔責任」，將責任外判至並無專業知識或無暇處理的居民，強調需再觀察日後相關部門有否確實執行制度。
梁浩軒又指，獨立委員會報告與早前聽證會上提及的情況大致一樣，報告亦「盡力還原事件」，並明確指出指出哪個部門須負責，唯一缺少的是因無權力傳召部分人士，未能解答在宏福苑個案中「有什麼人做了什麼導致成功圍標」。
阿詩（化名）的父母是宏福苑宏志閣居民，她則在大火前搬離，有相識的街坊逝世。
她留意記者會的情況後向BBC中文表示，「為何Day One不出來道歉」，認為李家超指災後有即時任務的說法不合理、亦非藉口，「你就算是多少事情要做，你說一句、鞠躬，我想十秒已夠了」。
她指，多名記者曾問及為何只有一名局長問責，但李家超沒有正面回應；她認為，目前尚有很多情況未完整交代，包括：「那個扔煙頭的人已抓到了嗎？」
妻子在宏福苑大火喪生的葉家駒表示，「她（何永賢）是辭職，我不知道辭職是叫『下台』」認為被報告點名部門的相關政策局的局長也應該下台，目前的行政問責並未足夠。他指，平日領功時局長有份，「出事時，局長沒份」，質疑為何標準「有趣」。
報告以遮蓋方式公開
特首李家超於去年12月宣佈成立由法官主持的「獨立委員會」，審視起火成因、監管人員角色和責任，以及工程是否涉貪圍標等問題。
委員會由高等法院原訟法庭法官陸啟康任主席。值得注意的是，獨立委員會與香港《調查委員會條例》下的「獨立調查委員會」不同，並不具法定權力，無法強制證人出庭作供和提交資料，一度引發市民對委員會能否徹查真相的擔憂。舉行聽證會期間，有部分人士不願意作供。
陸啟康其後解釋，獨立委員會的目的是找出事件經過及為何發生，個人追責由刑事及民事程序處理。他指出，若以法定調查方式調查個人責任，可能會令刑事及民事程序變得複雜及冗長，為檢控帶來更多不明朗的因素。而由於政府目標在9個月內完成工作，獨立委員會會較為靈活。
委員會於今年3月開始，在五個月內舉行30場聽證會，傳召80名證人及專家作供。10月22日，委員會向行政長官提交報告。
政府相隔一週後，以局部遮蓋內容方式公開。
李家超指，獨立委員會報告按律政司建議，將可能涉及相關刑事程序的內容部分遮蓋，以免影響有關刑事程序和保障公平審訊。
外界有聲音質疑政府延遲並遮蓋報告內容的做法。但過去類似事件的調查報告亦有類似做法。
2012年，香港南丫海難造成39人死亡。政府在公開法定調查委員會的報告前，由於涉事兩名船長已被控誤殺，為保障其獲得公平審訊的權利，決定遮蓋有關兩船長責任內容。
2018年大埔公路車禍發生後，政府委任獨立委員會調查事件，當時報告亦有遮蓋涉及刑事訴訟的相關內容。
政界一度流傳「刑不上局長」
去年12月，李家超在宣佈成立「獨立委員會」後多次強調「會問責到底、追責到底」，稱無論是政府或非政府、基層或高層，會公平地按事實追責懲處。
不過在報告公佈前，香港《明報》政治專欄曾引述政界人士消息稱，現屆政府任期僅剩八個月，官員現時下台難以另覓人選，「亦無意思」，認為「下屆政府不再任命，已是一種問責」。
該評論又援引建制人士分析，稱在目前香港的政治環境，即使追責「刑不上局長」，亦不會有暴動或示威遊行。行政會議成員湯家驊亦提出「錯失論」，指如司局長沒有犯錯，就不應問責下台。
說法傳出後迅速引起各方反彈。
前特區政府中央政策組首席顧問邵善波表示，「港人治港」的政府對市民有不可逃避責任。他指出，大火導致168人遇難及各種重大損失，形容無論放在任何標準下，「都不能算是一宗小事」，指中央及特區政府不採取任何政治問責，會對政府及整個制度的威信造成重大傷害。
多少涉案人士被捕？
大火發生後，香港警察與廉政公署成立聯合調查小組，循誤殺、工業意外、串謀詐騙及貪污等方向展開調查。
截至今年6月，警方及廉署分別拘捕39人及24人，包括工程顧問、承建商負責人、棚架工程分判商、業主立案法團成員、物業管理公司職員及中間人等。他們涉嫌誤殺、干犯賄賂、串謀詐騙、偽造帳目及俗稱「洗黑錢」等罪行。
今年6月10日，警方和廉署正式落案起訴其中七人及兩間公司，包括「誤殺罪」在內的25項控罪。
警方起訴鴻毅及宏業公司、三名時任董事與註冊檢驗人員，合共五項誤殺罪。廉署則同樣起訴上述兩間公司以及涉及工程的七名人員，當中包括串謀詐騙、洗黑錢、企圖妨礙司法公正，以及逃稅等20項控罪。
警方的拘捕行動並不僅限於維修工程人士，更包括市民及受災戶。
大火發生第三日，有市民成立「大埔宏福苑火災關注組」提出四大訴求發起聯署，當中包括成立獨立調查委員會、問責政府官員等。聯署發起人、24歲大學生關靖豐隨後被香港警察國安處拘捕，成為首個為災民發聲被捕的人。
另據香港本地媒體報導，前區議員張錦雄及一名女子、內容創作者Kenny Chan，亦被國安警察以煽動仇恨為由帶走調查。
國安警察亦拘捕並落案起訴前民間人權陣線副召集人王岸然香港《維護國安條例》下的「妨害調查危害國安罪行」罪與「發佈煽動刊物」罪，案件正於法院審理當中。
除此之外，曾揭發香港鐵路「沙中線」工程醜聞的吹哨人、建築工程商人潘焯鴻，在災後多次公開批評港府處理宏福苑善後。他於3月聽證會召開的前一日，被指涉及在2021年詐騙因新冠病毒病（COVID-19）疫情而設立的「百分百擔保特惠貸款計劃」，與妻子及4名公司員工被警方以涉嫌「串謀欺詐」罪拘捕。
以同一罪名被捕的還有宏福苑業主立案法團前委員江祥發。他在大火後積極接受傳媒訪問，並收集宏福苑業主聯署要求召開業主大會。今年5月，他被指涉詐騙「百份百擔保特惠貸款」，與妻子被控兩項「串謀欺詐」及一項「洗黑錢罪」。
江祥發獲准保釋後，曾向傳媒表示從今以後「不會接受任何訪問」。

items.title: 巴西前總統博索納羅之子敗給盧拉後，為何飛往美國？
items.description: 這位參議員離開巴西後，被拍到在美國走下飛機。他在巴西因涉嫌洗錢而接受調查。
items.content:
弗拉維奧·博索納羅：巴西前總統之子，敗給盧拉後，為何飛往美國？
  - Author, 路易斯·巴魯喬（Luis Barrucho）
  - Role, BBC國際部
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 5 分鐘
在巴西總統選舉中敗給總統路易斯·伊納西奧·盧拉·達席爾瓦（Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva；勞拉）僅數日後，落敗的挑戰者弗拉維奧·博索納羅（Flávio Bolsonaro；博爾索納羅）已離開巴西前往美國，儘管有法院命令要求他交出護照。週三（10月28日），有人目擊他在美國佛羅里達州下飛機。
這名右翼參議員因涉嫌洗錢正接受調查，他尚未被起訴，並否認有不當行為。
這一事件已引起全球關注，專家警告稱，此舉可能使巴西與美國總統唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump；川普）政府的關係進一步複雜化。
弗拉維奧·博索納羅是誰？
45歲的弗拉維奧·博索納羅是一名參議員，也是巴西前總統雅伊爾·博索納羅 (Jair Bolsonaro) 的長子。
他一直被視為父親的政治繼承人，在2026年總統選舉中成為右翼自由黨的候選人，並被廣泛認為是盧拉的接班人。
民調一直顯示，博索納羅的支持率領先盧拉或與盧拉持平。博索納羅贏得了第一輪投票，但在10月25日的總統決選中以微弱劣勢敗給了盧拉。
博索納羅拒絕承認敗選，反而要求宣布選舉結果無效，他認為延長選舉日的投票時間對他的對手不公平地有利。
巴西選舉當局已確認盧拉獲勝，最高選舉法院院長卡西奧·努內斯·馬克斯（Kássio Nunes Marques）——由博索納羅任命——表示，延長投票時間並未改變選舉結果。
博索納羅所在的政黨已經接受了選舉結果，但表示延長投票時間的決定值得進一步審查。
與此同時，博索納羅正面臨越來越多的法律挑戰。
他因涉嫌洗錢和其他金融犯罪正接受調查。當局也正在調查有關其總統競選活動涉及非法外國資金和干預的指控。他否認有任何不當行為，並稱對他的指控是出於政治動機。
他的參議員任期將於2027年初結束。卸任後，他將失去目前保護他免受某些形式起訴的議會保護。
他為什麼離開巴西？
離開巴西後，博索納羅在週三發表的首份聲明中表示：「我不是逃離巴西，我是為了巴西而離開。」
「我從來無意離開我的祖國，但我非常清楚事情將會朝哪個方向發展，」他說。
「我離開了一個非常時期的政權，好讓我能成為我的人民應得的領袖。」
他形容自己是一場政變和政治迫害的受害者，並表示他前往美國是為了保護家人。他還稱自己是巴西的「當選總統」，其後又稱自己是該國的「領袖」。
他感謝阿根廷總統哈維爾·米萊（Javier Milei）、特朗普以及美國人民，並表示他們與巴西「善良人民」擁有相同的價值觀。
週一（26日），巴西最高法院大法官亞歷山大·德莫賴斯（Alexandre de Moraes）要求博索納羅在24小時內交出護照，理由是他在接受調查期間有離境風險。作為現任參議員，博索納羅持有外交護照和普通護照。
在路透社看到的一份法院裁決中，最高法院以博索納羅有逃離巴西的風險及其「雄厚的財力」為由，下令扣押其護照。
博索納羅最初否認自己有意逃亡。
「我從未想過離開這個國家，」他在敗選後對記者表示。
但他錯過了交出護照的最後期限，巴西當局隨後註銷了這些證件。
然而，很快有報道稱，博索納羅可能在此之前已經離開了該國。
據阿根廷移民當局稱，博索納羅、他的妻子和兩個女兒於當地時間週二深夜越過巴西與阿根廷的陸路邊境，隨後登上一架飛往厄瓜多爾瓜亞基爾的私人飛機。
但厄瓜多爾當局尚未公開證實他已抵達，博索納羅本人及其代表也未透露其行蹤。
據信他從那裡動身前往美國。
週二（27日）早些時候，美國國務院一名高級官員告訴BBC，如果博索納羅及其家人提出申請，華盛頓將向他們發放簽證並允許他們入境。
週三，特朗普對記者表示：「我們讓他入境了」，但拒絕評論博索納羅聲明中的相關說法。
特朗普說：「我不會介入。那是一場非常奇怪的選舉，這是肯定的。」他接著補充稱，他認為博索納羅「以及他的家人受到了非常不公平的對待」。
盧拉則批評博索納羅，表示他本應留在巴西，為針對他的指控進行辯護。他補充說：「沒有任何事情需要隱瞞的人，就沒有任何事情需要害怕。」
最高法院下令博索納羅交出護照的決定本身也在巴西引發了爭議。
據《聖保羅頁報》（Folha de São Paulo）報道，盧拉政府的一些成員私下表示擔憂，認為此舉距選舉結果公佈不到24小時，可能被博索納羅的支持者視為出於政治動機，並加深兩極分化。
他們擔心，這可能會強化博索納羅陣營長期以來的說法，即巴西司法部門出於政治原因針對這個家族。
博索納羅家族為何與特朗普如此親近？
弗拉維奧·博索納羅突然前往美國，再次令人們關注博索納羅家族與特朗普之間長期以來的關係。
在擔任總統期間，雅伊爾·博索納羅與特朗普建立了密切關係，由於兩人政治風格和言論相似，他常被稱為「熱帶特朗普」。
特朗普一再支持博索納羅家族。
儘管他沒有公開為弗拉維奧·博索納羅的總統競選背書，但兩人在選戰期間於5月在白宮會面。
博索納羅後來表示，特朗普問及他的父親、前總統雅伊爾·博索納羅，並討論了有組織犯罪、關稅和關鍵礦產等問題。
在弗拉維奧·博索納羅敗選後，特朗普質疑選舉結果的合法性，稱這「看起來又是一場被操縱的選舉」。
他後來表示，如果博索納羅尋求在美國避難，他將表示歡迎。
「嗯，我會批准的。我認為他們是好人。那場選舉非常奇怪，我認為很糟糕。外界評價也很差。你看看他們的市場發生了什麼，」特朗普週三對記者說。
「我認為看到這一切太可怕了。你知道，我沒有偏袒任何一方。我認識他們兩個。我認識盧拉。我對弗拉維奧略知一二。我非常了解他的父親。我認為他父親受到了非常惡劣的對待，但我沒有參與其中。那是巴西，一個不同的國家，」他補充道。
在2022年敗給盧拉後，雅伊爾·博索納羅也前往了美國，而非立即承認敗選。
他後來返回巴西，因其支持者在巴西利亞衝擊政府大樓後策劃政變，被判處27年監禁。他目前正被軟禁。
弗拉維奧的弟弟愛德華多·博索納羅（Eduardo Bolsonaro）在成為巴西最高法院的調查對象後，於2025年3月移居美國。愛德華多稱自己是政治迫害的受害者，並在得克薩斯州（Texas）定居，成為博索納羅家族在華盛頓的主要發言人之一。
身在美國期間，他為父親和哥哥助選，與特朗普身邊的人物建立聯繫，並在涉及巴西的問題上遊說美國政界人士。
2025年12月，由於長期滯留國外，他失去了巴西眾議院（Chamber of Deputies）的席位。
今年6月，巴西最高法院裁定愛德華多在去年其父親的政變案審理期間尋求美國干預的罪名成立，但他拒絕接受這一裁決。
在今年大選前，愛德華多曾表示，如果哥哥敗選，他應該離開這個國家。
「如果我哥哥沒有獲勝，我贊成他離開這個國家，」他在美國接受保守派評論員史蒂文·克勞德（Steven Crowder）採訪時表示。
這對巴西與美國的關係意味著什麼？
這一事件發生在美洲兩個最大國家關係的敏感時刻。
巴西與美國的關係日益緊張，盧拉指責特朗普政府干預巴西選舉。
特朗普質疑選舉合法性的言論，加上華盛頓願意向博索納羅及其家人發放簽證，可能進一步加劇緊張局勢。
華盛頓智庫彼得森國際經濟研究所（Peterson Institute for International Economics）高級研究員莫妮卡·德博勒（Monica de Bolle）預計，巴西與美國的關係將保持「非常緊張」，巴西將在繼續推進外交的同時，對特朗普形成一種「地區性抵抗」。
但她認為，下個月的美國中期選舉可能會增加白宮面臨的壓力。
「如果民主黨獲勝，特朗普將不容易繼續與巴西作對，」她告訴BBC。
本文原以英文撰寫，我們使用了人工智能協助翻譯，並由BBC記者在發佈前進行審核。了解更多關於我們如何使用人工智能的資訊。

items.title: 以色列大選結束，內塔尼亞胡能否執政為何依然懸而未決？
items.description: 自1948 年建國以來，該國一直由聯合政府執政，但下一屆政府是否會包括現任總理內塔尼亞胡？
items.content:
以色列大選結束，內塔尼亞胡能否執政為何依然懸而未決？
自1948年建國以來，以色列一直由聯合政府領導，但下一屆政府是否會包括現任總理本雅明·內塔尼亞胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）？
這是自2023年10月7日哈馬斯主導襲擊以色列以來的首次大選，出口民調顯示，尚無明確贏家。
以色列兩家廣播電視機構預測，前軍方最高指揮官加迪·艾森科特（Gadi Eisenkot）領導的亞沙爾黨（Yashar）及其「變革聯盟」（Change Bloc）中的另外三個猶太人反對黨，將在擁有120個席位的以色列議會（Knesset）中贏得51席，與內塔尼亞胡領導的利庫德集團（Likud）及其極右翼和極端正統派猶太盟友的席位數相同。第三家廣播電視機構的民調則顯示，內塔尼亞胡領先三席。
局勢在很大程度上將取決於兩個阿拉伯人政黨發揮的作用，預測顯示它們將贏得創紀錄的18或19席。
10月27日的投票率創下數十年來新高。
但接下來會發生什麼？
以色列的選舉制度是如何運作的？
以色列議會稱為「克奈塞特」（Knesset），共有120席，這意味著任何政府必須掌握61席才能取得多數。
以色列採用比例代表制選舉制度，因此政府歷來都是由多個政黨組成的聯合政府。
以下是本屆議會在大選前、由內塔尼亞胡聯盟執政時的席位分佈。
以下是目前的局勢。
內塔尼亞胡能否組成政府？
週二大選的最終結果確認後，以色列總統將在與所有政治派別磋商後，邀請他認為最有可能成功的政黨領袖組建執政聯盟。這一過程可能需要數週。
通常，總統會任命獲得最多議會席位的政黨領袖組閣。目前擔任總統的是伊薩克·赫爾佐格（Isaac Herzog）。但這並非硬性規定：例如，2009年大選後，時任總統西蒙·佩雷斯（Shimon Peres）首先邀請內塔尼亞胡組閣，儘管他領導的利庫德集團所得席位少於對手前進黨（Kadima）。
總統首位指定的組閣人選最多有42天時間組建政府。如果未能成功，另一名政黨領袖將獲得機會。
如果沒有任何政黨能夠取得過半數席位，也可能由少數派政府執政。如果這也行不通，則可能重新舉行選舉，在此之前內塔尼亞胡將繼續擔任看守總理。
哪些政黨參與角逐？
預測顯示，內塔尼亞胡的利庫德集團和艾森科特的亞沙爾黨將成為議會中的兩大黨，但它們需要其他政黨的支持才能組建聯合政府。內塔尼亞胡領導的是一個由右翼和宗教政黨組成的聯盟。
他於1996年首次上台。在伊扎克·拉賓（Yitzhak Rabin）遇刺後提前舉行的選舉中，他成為以色列首位直接選舉產生的總理，並在過去30年的大部分時間裡執政。
艾森科特領導的反對派聯盟由中右翼和左傾政黨組成，主要因取代內塔尼亞胡這一共同目標而團結起來。
該聯盟包括前總理納夫塔利·貝內特（Naftali Bennett）領導的比亞哈德黨（B'Yachad）。
另有兩個阿拉伯人政黨聯盟參選，以色列約五分之一的人口是阿拉伯人。理論上，它們可能成為決定誰能執政的關鍵力量。但在主要猶太人政黨中，除一個政黨外，其餘均已排除與它們共同執政的可能性。
何時能知道結果？
初步結果預計於10月28日公佈。估計有60萬張缺席選票，主要由軍人投下，約佔總票數的10％，要到週四才能全部點算完畢。正式結果定於11月4日公佈。
聯合政府的談判過程可能需要數週，甚至數月。2021年3月大選後，直到6月才組建政府，由貝內特與亞伊爾·拉皮德（Yair Lapid）達成權力分享協議。
當時，內塔尼亞胡首先獲得組閣機會，但未能組建可行的執政聯盟。
重新舉行選舉並不罕見——2019年至2022年間，由於各黨無法就合作達成一致，以色列先後舉行了五次選舉。

items.title: 印中關係緩和之際：印邊境官員稱中國軍隊大批集結並搭帳篷
items.description: 印中關係原本正處於謹慎的復甦階段，直到一位邊境官員的言論引發了人們對實際情況的新疑慮。
items.content:
印中關係緩和之際：印邊境官員稱中國軍隊大批集結並搭帳篷
  - Author, 安巴拉桑·埃希拉揚（Anbarasan Ethirajan）
  - Role, BBC 全球事務記者
- Published
- 閱讀時間: 4 分鐘
在過去一年的大部分時間裡，印中關係似乎走在一條謹慎的復甦之路上。
數十年來，兩國關係起起伏伏——尤其是在存在爭議的喜馬拉雅邊界問題上。
但過去幾天的事態表明，自2020年最近一次衝突以來出現的解凍，可能比表面上更加脆弱。
最新的擔憂始於印度邊境警察部隊負責人表示，今年早些時候，中國軍隊大批返回喜馬拉雅邊境的爭議地區，並在印度主張擁有的領土內數公里處搭起帳篷。
印藏邊境警察部隊（Indo-Tibetan Border Police，ITBP）總監沙特魯吉特·辛格·卡普爾（Shatrujeet Singh Kapur）的這番言論，在德里（Delhi）引發了一場政治爭議。
首先，現任官員發表此類言論實屬罕見。敏感的邊境問題通常由聯邦政府通過其國防部或外交部處理。
卡普爾最近在拉賈斯坦邦（Rajasthan）的一次官員集會上表示，印中兩軍曾在東北部的阿魯納恰爾邦（Arunachal Pradesh）多個地點發生對峙，而且對峙仍在持續。
他說，對抗始於7月，但雙方最初都撤離了。
他補充說，幾天後，中國軍隊以更大規模返回，並在「印度所認知的實際控制線（Line of Actual Control，LAC）以內約六到七公里處」搭起了帳篷。
實際控制線是一條分隔兩個鄰國各自控制區域的模糊界線，印中兩國圍繞這條長達3,440公里（2,100英里）的爭議邊界已爭執了數十年。
中國宣稱阿魯納恰爾邦是藏南地區的一部分。但德里一直拒絕接受這一主張，稱該邦是印度不可分割的一部分。
這場爭端是1947年獨立的印度從英國殖民統治中繼承的最棘手挑戰之一。它曾導致1962年一場短暫的邊境戰爭，印度在戰爭中遭受了屈辱性的失敗。
六十多年後，大部分邊界仍未劃定，兩國維持著相互重疊的領土主張。
該地區崎嶇的地形使問題更加複雜：河道變遷、湖泊和積雪覆蓋的山峰，都令難以確立清晰的邊界。
因此，雙方軍隊可能在邊境線上迎面相遇，有時會引發暴力衝突和外交緊張。
上一次重大升級發生在2020年6月，當時印中軍隊在拉達克（Ladakh）的加勒萬河谷（Galwan Valley）發生衝突。至少20名印度士兵和4名中國士兵喪生。
這是自1975年以來雙方首次發生致命對抗。印度反對黨指責政府將領土拱手讓給中國——總理納倫德拉·莫迪（Narendra Modi）領導的政府一再駁斥這一說法。
衝突導致兩國關係急劇惡化，外交接觸中斷，貿易和人員往來受到影響。經過多輪談判，兩個鄰國於2024年同意採取措施緩和邊境緊張局勢。
此後，雙方著手恢復直航，並放寬衝突後實施的簽證限制。
中國國家主席習近平9月也訪問印度出席金磚國家（BRICS）峰會，這是他七年來首次訪印。
這些事態發展令人們對兩國關係更廣泛的正常化燃起了希望。但最新報道的對峙事件，令人重新質疑實地究竟取得了多少進展。
卡普爾發表言論後，主要反對黨國大黨（Congress）再次指責莫迪對北京作出讓步。
國大黨資深領袖賈伊拉姆·拉梅什（Jairam Ramesh）在X上寫道：「總理及其整個執政機器對這一嚴重問題保持沉默。」
對於卡普爾所稱中國軍隊在印度視為實際控制線己方一側數公里處搭起帳篷的說法，印度政府並未明確否認。
外交部發言人蘭迪爾·賈伊斯瓦爾（Randhir Jaiswal）上週表示，「當中國軍隊偏離既定的巡邏模式時，邊境地區的局勢就會不時受到干擾」。
他說，兩國正通過軍事和外交渠道處理懸而未決的問題，但沒有透露更多細節。
中國外交部一名發言人表示，中國「一貫嚴格遵守」與印度達成的相關協議，並在邊境地區開展「正常的巡邏和管理活動，以維護領土主權」。
專家表示，卡普爾的言論罕見地揭示了中國在爭議邊境沿線日益強勢的軍事姿態。
曾在2000年代中期主持多輪對華邊界談判的印度前外交秘書希亞姆·薩蘭（Shyam Saran）告訴BBC：「中國在阿魯納恰爾邦邊境多個地點進行試探的這種模式，已經持續了一段時間。」
他說，此類行動「不足以立即引發戰爭，但足以在地面上造成某種新的既成事實」。
印度反對黨長期以來指責中國擴大在拉達克和阿魯納恰爾邦的存在，導致局勢緊張。
中國人民解放軍（People's Liberation Army）退役大校、現任職於清華大學（Tsinghua University）的周波表示，兩國都從2020年加勒萬衝突中吸取了教訓。
「雙方應更加謹慎，避免今後再發生此類事件，」他說，並補充稱中國媒體沒有報道最近在阿魯納恰爾邦發生的對峙。
印中緊張關係的背景，還有一段複雜的經濟關係。
儘管存在分歧，兩國仍是主要貿易夥伴，去年雙邊貿易額達到1,510億美元。但貿易天平嚴重向北京傾斜，中國對印度的出口約佔1,310億美元。
印度在機械、稀土磁鐵、電動汽車電池和醫藥產品方面仍依賴從中國進口。
這種依賴意味著與北京的緊張關係可能帶來遠超邊境範圍的後果，尤其是對印度的工業和基礎設施項目而言。
上週，中國還宣布限制用於地鐵和公路建設的隧道掘進機出口，稱此舉旨在保護國家安全和國家利益。雖然這些限制並非專門針對印度，但會對印度的基礎設施建設計劃產生影響。
紐約州立大學奧爾巴尼分校（University at Albany）教授克里斯托弗·克拉里（Christopher Clary）告訴BBC：「中國對印度的政策旨在使印度崛起複雜化，包括印度掌握先進技術與製造業某些領域的能力。」
去年也出現過類似問題，當時中國限制了稀土磁鐵的出口——稀土磁鐵廣泛用於電動汽車、智能手機、風力發電機和醫療掃描儀。
此舉一度給印度工業造成供應問題，凸顯北京對關鍵材料的控制如何影響全球供應鏈。
印度目前正努力建立稀土磁鐵的本土生產能力，但發展這一產業需要時間和投資。
對於生活在爭議邊境沿線的人們來說，與中國關係緊張的後果更為直接。
《阿魯納恰爾時報》（Arunachal Times）資深記者通厄姆·里娜（Tongam Rina）說：「生活在一些邊境地區的村民告訴我們，由於中國的侵入和蠶食，他們無法進入草場。這不是什麼新鮮事，已經發生很長時間了。」
她補充說，這在「當地民眾中造成了一種不安全感」。
村民通常不會再回到那些「禁止進入的」地區狩獵和放牧犛牛，他們也不確定何時才會再獲准進入。
這場邊境爭端對德里還有更廣泛的戰略影響。越來越多人意識到，唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump）總統專注於擴大與中國的經濟接觸，這可能限制華盛頓在未來任何與北京的對抗中支持印度的意願。
分析人士說，中國可能對與印度發生全面衝突興趣不大，但它或許認為讓爭端持續下去有利可圖。
隨著中國經濟和軍事實力的增強，它可能會盤算，長期僵持將增強其在未來任何談判中的地位。
對印度來說，最近的對峙提醒人們：外交關係的改善，未必能轉化為邊境的持久穩定。

items.title: 德语媒体：“普特习”联盟并不可怕
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：-普特习-联盟并不可怕/a-79799002?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 《新苏黎世报》评论称，有关举行中美俄三方首脑峰会的建议，确实引发了超级大国划分世界的担忧。但上述三国并不可能成为持久的盟友。《柏林日报》认为，德国总统和总理同时展开的亚洲之行反映了德国对华政策的两难境地。
items.content:
（德国之声中文网）《新苏黎世报》评论认为，对华盛顿来说，有关今年十一月举行中美俄三方首脑会谈的建议，可以说来得正是时候：特朗普身边智囊们梦寐以求的中美俄结盟愿景正在初具雏形。按照这一愿景，中美俄三大核军事强国将划分各自的势力范围、彼此尊重、并依照自身利益统治世界其他地区。那么，真有可能出现这样的三强联手吗？这篇题为《不必惧怕普京、特朗普和习近平》的评论写道：
“特朗普的权势开始走下坡路之际，莫斯科提出了召开三方峰会的建议，这绝非偶然。在美国，特朗普的支持率已经跌至谷底，居高不下的通胀令美国民众苦不堪言，而高利率更是给消费者和企业带来了极大的负担。与此同时，特朗普朋友圈正在大发横财的消息却不绝于耳。
外交层面上，特朗普的处境也不太理想。他满口承诺的乌克兰和平迟迟未能实现，伊朗战争也依然看不到尽头。美国军事力量已经露出疲惫之态，而全球能源市场的局势也变得越来越紧张。美国的传统盟友不知所措之际，美国的国际信誉正在直线下跌。
有鉴于此，北京和莫斯科当权者想借机利用美国虚弱期的风险当然是存在的，特朗普也确实为他们提供了大量的机会，他甚至想把乌克兰当成送给俄罗斯的大礼。但尽管如此，特朗普身边战略家们梦寐以求的新世界秩序是否能应运而生，仍值得高度怀疑。”
《新苏黎世报》评论指出，同冷战时期的苏联相比，今天的俄罗斯早已算不上超级大国，对世界的影响力也非常有限。而随着俄乌战争的持续，俄罗斯对中国的依赖也在与日俱增。
“相比之下，北京正在巧妙地扩展其势力范围。尽管中国在加紧扩充军备，但却在尽可能避免使用武力。外交和出口攻势相辅相成，为中国建立起了遍布全球的贸易网络，并为中国的快速崛起奠定了基础。中国成了全球化的最大受益者，而这本身也是中国的软肋所在。
中国的外贸成就离不开遍布全球的贸易伙伴。对中国而言，欧盟市场以及亚洲邻国市场要比美俄市场更具规模。失去了上述伙伴，中国的崛起进程将戛然而止，本已危机四伏的国内经济更会陷入瘫痪。北京的领导层会不惜一切代价避免这种局面的出现。有鉴于此，中小型国家要利用这一机会，他们不仅对北京有经济影响力，也应当确实发挥这种影响力，欧盟尤为如此。
在美国，尽管特朗普仍在当政，但美国要同中俄等两大世界专制政权结成联盟还远不是铁板钉钉的事情。特朗普在推行短视而残酷的、唯利是图的政治，其MAGA阵营中仇视欧洲者也的确大有人在。但他们的立场并不能代表整个美国。特朗普对普京和习近平莫名其妙的好感，令绝大多数美国人感到无法理解。有鉴于此，它也不可能成为美国外交政策的常态。
新的世界秩序将是一个强弱共存的多极世界。国际法准则的约束力虽然被打了折扣，但全球范围内利益和资源分配的多元性，使得中美俄三个军事强权无法主导世界。”
德国对华政策：对抗与务实的平衡
德国总统施泰因迈尔对中国展开国事访问的同时，德国总理默茨则访问了新加坡、日本和韩国等中国的重要邻国。《柏林日报》评论写道：
”过去，作为软实力强大的斡旋者，德国总是试图平衡各方利益。既能同各方保持对话渠道，也能同不好打交道的对手建立信任，总之，同各方开展经济合作一直是德国外交政策的招牌。在那时，同基辅、莫斯科、新德里、伊斯兰堡、德黑兰或者耶路撒冷同时坐在谈判席上，对德国来说，并不是一件难事。从这个意义上讲，施泰因迈尔和默茨同时展开的亚洲之行，更像是那个意识形态还较为淡漠年代的事情。
然而，这种双轨战略也有其局限性。中国可能会将德国加强与日韩关系的努力视为其遏制中国政策的一部分。但另一方面，如果对依赖提出警告的同时，却不去寻找切实可行的经济替代方案，柏林的信誉必将大大折扣。
因此，要成功维持这种平衡，必须满足三个条件：德国的对华政策必须保持可预期性，德国必须切实落实经济关系的多元化，在公平竞争的问题上，德国必须坚持原则。”

items.description: 德国总统施泰因迈尔在北京大学呼吁德中携手合作，共同加强基于规则的国际秩序，倡导和平与全球自由贸易。
items.content:
德国总统：国家越大、实力越强，责任也就越重大
2026年10月29日
广告
（德国之声中文网）周四（10月29日）他在北京大学接受荣誉教授头衔后，发表演讲指出，当前的国际秩序正面临前所未有的冲击。“我们面临着陷入无序状态的风险，这对我们所有人而言都是巨大的危险。”
正在访华的德国总统还呼吁在中德之间以及中欧之间，建立公平的贸易竞争环境。他说，近年来，中国努力实现尽可能高度的独立，这是一个可以理解的目标。但是，“中国对经济更独立自主的追求，绝不能导致其他国家对中国的依赖性和脆弱性随之增加。”
施泰因迈尔表示，欧洲无法接受自身经济陷入这种单方面的脆弱境地，“正如中国也不会接受同样境地一样。”
他强调，德国不希望与中国脱钩，而是希望在更加公平的条件下继续合作。
施泰因迈尔敦促中国履行其作为全球大国的责任，他说，“国家越大、实力越强，责任也就越重大”。
协助结束俄罗斯对乌克兰发动的侵略战争。他表示，“中国是联合国安理会常任理事国，且与俄罗斯保持密切联系，让我们共同努力，促使俄罗斯停止侵略，进入严肃的谈判进程。”
施泰因迈尔还呼吁，全球社会应携手应对所面临的重大挑战，比如在气候与环境保护方面，以及如何对待人工智能。

items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/俄非峰会闭幕　普京称俄非为-天然盟友/a-79798490?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 第三届俄罗斯-非洲峰会周四在莫斯科闭幕。近50个非洲国家与会，其中约20国由领导人出席。普京称俄非是建设多极世界秩序的"天然盟友"，支持非洲获得联合国安理会常任理事国席位，并强调俄罗斯在粮食、化肥、教育和军事合作方面对非洲的援助。
items.content:
俄非峰会闭幕 普京称俄非为"天然盟友"
2026年10月29日
（德国之声中文网）周四（10月29日），俄罗斯-非洲峰会落下帷幕。俄罗斯总统普京在峰会上拉拢数十位非洲领导人，力图扩大莫斯科在非洲大陆的影响力。
普京在峰会第二天于克里姆林宫举行的会议上说，俄罗斯和非洲由"真正牢固的友谊和密切的伙伴关系"联结在一起。他说，双方是建设一个"多极、真正民主"世界秩序的"天然盟友"，这一秩序应摆脱强权和双重标准，以尊重国际法准则和《联合国宪章》基本原则为基础。他还提到苏联时期莫斯科对非洲国家反殖民斗争的支持。
力挺非洲获安理会常任席位
非洲拥有近16亿人口，在国际舞台上的影响力日益增强，其54个国家构成联合国最大的投票集团。莫斯科曾于2019年和2023年举办俄非峰会。本届峰会吸引了近50个非洲国家参加，其中约20国由领导人出席。
肯尼亚总统鲁托（William Ruto）在会上说，国际秩序必须反映当今世界，而不是1945年的世界，非洲不能继续没有联合国安理会的常任席位。普京当即表示支持，称安理会没有非洲代表"是不公平的"。埃及总统塞西则强调，非洲的安全与稳定是实现非洲人民愿望的必要条件。
粮食、化肥与军事合作
普京说，去年俄罗斯与非洲国家的贸易额超过270亿美元，并承诺继续扩大。他称，俄罗斯企业以平等、诚信的方式与非洲伙伴合作，不像昔日帝国那样以殖民方式"抽走利润"，而是把收益再投资于当地经济、分享先进技术、创造就业。
普京还说，俄罗斯去年向非洲供应了1800多万吨粮食，今年前九个月又供应了1300万吨，称这是对非洲粮食安全的"实实在在的贡献"。去年俄罗斯对非洲的化肥出口约150万吨，今年迄今已超过220万吨。目前，约有4万名非洲学生在俄罗斯大学就读。
普京特别强调，俄罗斯帮助非洲国家维护内部稳定与安全、加强国防和执法能力，并已与45个非洲国家签署了军事和军事技术合作政府间协议。
在与美国、欧洲和中国争夺非洲影响力的过程中，俄罗斯还借助军事承包商，在经济、安全和政治等多个领域扩大自身影响。

items.title: 默茨韩国之行：“我们深知生活在一个分裂的国家是多么痛苦”
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/默茨韩国之行：-我们深知生活在一个分裂的国家是多么痛苦/a-79798077?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 德国总理默茨在首尔与韩国总统李在明共同举行了联合新闻发布会，默茨表示，两国关系将提升至“深层战略伙伴关系”的水平。他说，在全球动荡时期，“我们现在加深伙伴关系是理所应当”。
items.content:
默茨韩国之行：“我们深知生活在一个分裂的国家是多么痛苦”
2026年10月29日
（德国之声中文网）韩国之行是默茨此次亚洲之旅的最后一站。本周四（10月29日），德国总理默茨同韩国总统李在明宣布，两国关系上升到深层的战略伙伴关系。在谈到俄罗斯对乌克兰的侵略战争时，默茨总理指出，拥有共同利益和价值观的伙伴，比以往任何时候都更加重要：“这适用于安全政策、经济和地缘政治。”
默茨表示，“我们之所以紧密相连，是因为我们都曾亲身经历过地缘政治紧张与分裂所带来的考验。我们深知，生活在一个分裂的国家是多么痛苦。”
默茨透露，他将前往韩朝边界的非军事区，同当地民众进行交流。他说，“韩国的安全关乎欧洲的安全，而欧洲的安全也同样影响着韩国的安全。这一点显而易见，例如，当朝鲜士兵在顿巴斯地区与乌克兰作战时，这便构成了对整个欧洲自由的威胁；而莫斯科向平壤提供武器，同样会带来相应的后果。”他总结道，世界正在变得更“小”了，即便是在战争时期。
欧韩合作是真正成功的典范
根据两国发布的联合声明，德国和韩国计划在安全和国防领域加强信息交流，两国都希望为各自地区及其周边的稳定、安全和繁荣做出贡献。声明称，德韩两国反对暴力和破坏稳定的行为，包括外国干涉。多年来，韩国一直与受中国和俄罗斯支持的朝鲜存在着紧张关系。
默茨表示，德国和韩国都是具备防范能力的民主国家，坚信只有基于规则的国际秩序，才能确保持续繁荣。他称15年前签署的欧盟与韩国的自由贸易协定，是“真正成功的典范”，双边大约99%的关税被取消。自2011年以来，双边贸易额增长了一倍多。
默茨总理在首尔还宣布了一项新的框架协议，并将之称作“尖端技术合作的基础”。双方计划在半导体行业开展合作，明年在柏林举行的德国数字峰会，李在明总统已确认韩国参加。此外，双方将在人工智能安全议题上展开合作。
多年来，韩国一直是德国在亚洲的最重要的经济伙伴之一。韩国芯片制造占据着全球领先地位，随着人工智能的蓬勃发展，芯片的重要性会进一步提升。柏林加强与韩国的合作，也是为降低对中国的依赖。
访问韩国之后，默茨的亚洲之行也告一段落。抵达首尔前，默茨总理访问了日本和新加坡。来自工业、科技、能源和国防领域的代表陪同了默茨总理的亚洲之旅。

items.title: 中国官媒连番炮轰  Hello Kitty母公司也为"辱华"道歉
items.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中国官媒连番炮轰-hello-kitty母公司也为-辱华-道歉/a-79796271?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
items.description: 日本TBS电视台谍战剧《VIVANT》第二季描写中国情报人员对日本特工施以酷刑，被央视批评为"抹黑中国"。Hello Kitty母公司三丽鸥因与该剧推出联名玩偶，遭中国官方媒体接连点名，其中国子公司周三深夜在微博致歉，宣布终止合作。中国外交部称，该剧暴露出日本有一股势力企图通过文化产品丑化中国。部分中国网民则对这场风波冷嘲热讽。
items.content:
中国官媒连番炮轰 Hello Kitty母公司也为"辱华"道歉
2026年10月29日
（德国之声中文网）Hello Kitty母公司三丽鸥（Sanrio）的中国子公司周三（10月28日）宣布，终止与日本谍战剧《VIVANT》的联名合作。此前，该合作在中国社交媒体上引发持续不满，中国官方媒体本周加大了谴责力度。这是几天内第二起类似事件，凸显外国企业和名人在中国市场如履薄冰。
风波缘起：谍战剧被指"抹黑中国"
《VIVANT》（中文又称《别班》）由日本TBS电视台制作，堺雅人、阿部宽等主演，也在奈飞（Netflix）上播出。据报道，正在播出的第二季中，出现中国情报人员对日本特工施以酷刑的情节。
中国官方媒体对这部剧进行了猛烈批评。据报道，央视指责该剧"把中国人拍成惨无人道的施暴者，把日本自卫队情报人员美化成正义反击者"，称剧中断指、刺腹等酷刑与侵华日军的手段相似，是将日军罪行"嫁接"到中国身上，对观众进行"认知投毒"。
TBS社长龙宝正峰周三在例行记者会上表示，这部剧"完全是虚构的，无意贬低任何特定国家"。
据媒体报道，三丽鸥今年7月已与该剧推出首批联名玩偶，让Hello Kitty、美乐蒂等角色换上剧中人物的服装；10月下旬，双方宣布第二批合作产品将发售，争议随之扩大。
官媒炮轰：从"不应与右翼共舞"到"玩火者必自焚"
《环球时报》28日发表评论《Hello Kitty不应与日本右翼共舞》，称三丽鸥与该剧合作背离了其"可爱""治愈"的品牌形象，也背离了创始人"人人和睦相处"的理念。评论还特别提到，三丽鸥2026年上半年在中国的收入达7.81亿元人民币，同比增长超过四成。多个官方媒体微博账号随即转发，相关话题登上微博热搜。
三丽鸥（上海）国际贸易有限公司28日深夜在官方微博发表声明，称此次联名"包含与三丽鸥集团企业理念不符的表达"，决定终止合作及后续宣传，并将加强审核机制。
这份声明起初只在微博以中文发布。北京日报客户端29日发表评论，质疑这是"特供道歉"、缺乏诚意。评论称该剧是"辱华毒剧"，警告日本军国主义正通过文化产品向青少年"投毒"，并表示"玩火者必自焚"。三丽鸥随后于29日下午在日本官网补发了日文版声明。观察者网援引日本媒体报道称，TBS官方购物网站上的相关联名商品页面已无法显示。
外交部表态：“暴露出日本国内始终存在一股势力”
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆29日在例行记者会上回应称，这部电视剧"再次暴露出日本国内始终存在一股势力，企图通过文化产品丑化、抹黑中国，散播仇华情绪"，应当引起国际社会和日本国内有识之士的警惕。
网民反讽与外企困境：极度自卑导致极度敏感？
官方媒体的批评也招致部分中国网民的反讽。有网民说"极度自卑才会导致极度敏感"，还有人质问："自己允许有抗日神剧，不允许人家有抗中神剧？"
自日本首相高市早苗去年底就台湾问题发表言论以来，中日关系急剧恶化，中国已劝阻本国公民赴日旅游，并收紧对日稀土出口。但包括三丽鸥在内的大批日本企业仍依赖中国市场。几天前，法国球星姆巴佩刚因涉及“毛泽东是独裁者”的言论致歉，多家中国赞助商已与他解约。此前，杜嘉班纳（Dolce & Gabbana）、H&M、耐克和阿迪达斯等外国品牌，也曾因“辱华”言论或者涉及“抵制新疆棉花”或表达对“强迫劳动”关切在中国遭遇抵制。

Patrick Stewart, of Star Trek and X-Men fame, dies at 86
While best known for his on-screen roles as Professor X and Captain Picard, the veteran actor spent much of his career on stage
Patrick Stewart, who rose from poverty in England to become an accomplished Shakespearean stage actor and then achieved global stardom as the erudite Captain Jean-Luc Picard in television’s Star Trek: The Next Generation and the telepathic Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, has died at the age of 86.
Stewart, knighted in 2010 by Queen Elizabeth for his contributions to drama, died at his home in Los Angeles, according to a statement on his social media account.
“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” it said.

“According to initial findings, two people were killed and five others injured in the incident,” Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said on social media.

US bans Chinese labs from testing electronics ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
The FCC measure targets testing facilities with alleged PLA ties, giving US labs until December 2028 to expand capacity
The United States on Thursday banned all Chinese laboratories from testing electronic devices destined for the US market, just weeks before US President Donald Trump is due to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.
The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) voted to bar testing laboratories and certification bodies in China and other economies that lack a “mutual recognition agreement” or reciprocal trade agreement with the US.
“This is consistent with President Trump’s broader effort to restore balance and fairness with respect to America’s dealings with foreign nations,” said FCC Chairman Brendan Carr.

items.title: Burnham says he wants to cut welfare bill 'as soon as we possibly can'
items.description: Opponents have questioned the Budget's lack of detail on welfare reform, with the prime minister not outlining a timetable for any reductions.
items.content:
Burnham says he wants to cut welfare bill 'as soon as we possibly can'
- Published
Andy Burnham has said he wants to cut the welfare bill "as soon as we possibly can", but was unable to guarantee this would happen before the next general election.
Opponents raised concerns over the lack of details on welfare reform in Wednesday's Budget, after welfare spending was forecast to increase from £353bn this year to £431bn in 2031/32.
Asked whether he would seek to reduce the bill before the next election, Burnham told reporters: "We want to get the welfare bill down as quickly as possible, and we're working flat out to that end."
He warned against "crude cuts" and said he wants to get people into "sustainable employment". The Conservatives accused Labour of being "addicted to welfare".
- Budget 2026: Key points at a glance 
  - Published1 day ago
The prime minister faced questions about his approach after the Treasury disputed that Chancellor John Healey had suggested to the BBC that the benefits bill will be cut before the next election, which must be held by August 2029.
When Healey was asked by the Today Programme on Radio 4 whether there would be a cut in the bill before polling day, he said: "There will be, there will be a reduction in the benefits bill, we'll do that in a Labour way."
But several Treasury sources took issue with this being interpreted as a promise to do so by the next election. Downing Street later said it was "not setting an arbitrary target or timetable".
The prime minister's official spokesman would not say whether the government's ambition to cut welfare spending meant reducing it below its current level, or ensuring that future spending rises at a slower rate than is currently projected.
Further details about the government's proposals are expected after two major reports are published in November.
These include a review of disability benefits co-chaired by Labour minister Sir Stephen Timms and one on young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) led by former minister Alan Milburn.
The two reviews were announced by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer after his attempt to make significant changes to the welfare system, including restricting eligibility for some health-related benefits, resulted in a mass revolt of Labour MPs and an embarrassing climbdown in June 2025.
Speaking during a visit to Derby, Burnham said the "big next priority in front of us" is the publication of the Milburn report.
He said: "We just want to get stuck into supporting people to help people off benefits and into work. There's no delay there. We want that to happen as quickly as possible."
Pressed again for a timeline on his plans, the prime minister said: "We're working hard to cut the welfare bill as soon as we possibly can. But we're doing it in a way that supports people into work.
"If we just went and made crude cuts, in the end, that leaves people in crisis, and you spend more public money somewhere else, so it's about getting people into sustainable employment."
'Huge bonus'
Former Bank of England chief economist Andy Haldane said if the government could provide a plan to show "greater restraint" of the benefits bill, that would "play spectacularly well" with the financial markets.
Haldane, who has previously advised Burnham, told the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson podcast: "If the government could get that through I think it would come with a huge bonus."
Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch responded to the Budget by saying the country was "overspent, overborrowed, overtaxed, and drowning in an out-of-control welfare system".
Reacting to government briefings and remarks on Thursday related to when a reduction in the benefits bill could take place, Badenoch said it "looks like foot in mouth syndrome is spreading".
She said: "Don't let anyone tell you this was a 'do no harm budget'. In doing so little, Labour have harmed our economic security and they've harmed our national security."
Welfare spending is forecast to rise this year by £19bn to £353bn.
Watchdog and forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said this figure is expected to rise to £431bn in 2031/32, driven primarily by health-related and pensioner benefit spending.
Of the figure forecast for 2031/32, £209.8bn is on pensioners, including the state pension and winter fuel payments, while £110.7bn is on universal credit and legacy equivalents and £69.6bn is on disability benefits such as personal independence payments.
The government has already pledged to reform the existing state pension triple lock from 2030, and more proposals and changes to the welfare system are expected to emerge in the coming months.

items.title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall
items.description: Budget forecasts show growth in living standards grinding almost to a halt.
items.content:
'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall
- Published
People are facing a "painful" and "depressing" few years ahead, economic think tanks have warned, after forecasts showed growth in living standards grinding almost to a halt.
Typical working-age households would see their disposable income fall by £1,050, or 3%, between now and 2029, according to the Resolution Foundation, while the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the current decade would be the worst for household income growth on record.
Chancellor John Healey said his Budget offered "breathing space", but said the government could "never remove completely" cost of living pressures.
The UK's official forecaster said its latest economic forecast painted a "pretty grim picture".
The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), blamed the difficult financial situation facing the UK on higher borrowing costs and inflation caused by the US-Iran war.
In response to rising energy prices, Healey has announced measures, including a £100 support payment, aimed at easing pressure on household finances.
But that would not be enough to offset the impact of higher energy bills, the Resolution Foundation said.
"This parliament is increasingly looking like one of two halves," said the think tank's chief executive, Ruth Curtice.
"The first half has been marked by rising living standards, solid economic growth and extra funding for public services," she said.
However, the second half of the parliament would be "tough going", she said.
- Treasury will not commit to reducing welfare bill before next election 
  - Published9 hours ago
- What we now know about the UK economy in four charts 
  - Published1 day ago
- Your pay, energy bills and savings: How the Budget affects you 
  - Published5 hours ago
In response to this "painful" situation the government had provided a "scattergun" Budget that did not do enough to address the challenges facing the country, Curtice said.
Over the course of this parliament, incomes for non-pensioner households, after taxes, benefits, and housing costs are taken into account, will have risen by "a paltry" £600, the Resolution Foundation said, with the gains "already behind us".
Even after the extra support provided by the government, households will be left paying higher energy bills than during the last energy crisis in 2022, according to its analysis.
The Resolution Foundation said the support should have been more targeted at the poorest households.
Lost decade
Alongside the Budget the OBR issued its economic forecast indicating a slowdown in GDP growth from 1.2% in 2026 to 1% in 2027.
The forecast for next year is sharply lower than what was predicted at their last assessment in March.
The OBR also put its forecast for inflation for 2027 up from 2% to 3.4%.
Frozen tax thresholds are also eating into people's take-home pay.
However, the OBR also emphasised the difficulties in economic forecasting, highlighting uncertainty over the future path of inflation, in particular, which could turn out to be either significantly higher or lower than their predictions.
While the Resolution Foundation focused its forecast for living standards on working age households, the OBR looks at all households, including pensioners and reflects a 10-year rolling average growth to take into account short-term fluctuations.
The OBR found that by the end of the decade living standards for all households would have barely grown, by less than 0.1% per year.
Helen Miller, director of the influential think tank, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the outlook was "depressing".
"This decade looks set to be the worst decade for growth in household incomes on record," she said.
"No amount of temporary cost of living packages will fix that. We need a stronger economy."
'Fragile' finances
There would also be growing pressure on the government's spending plans over the parliament, Miller added.
"Spending plans look extremely tight. They don't look to me like plans that this government would want to deliver," she said.
"Whether or not they are delivered matters because the spending plans underpin the plan to bring down borrowing," she added.
Miller said she was left with the impression that Healey was hoping the economy would improve to take the pressure off those spending decisions.
Healey, speaking on the BBC's Today Programme, said "economic storms", including the Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, were affecting countries around the world and the government was seeking to help where it could.
He said energy bill help would create "breathing space" for most households.
Around 20 million households are set to receive the £100 payment based on which council tax band they are in.
But Conservative shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said the Budget had left the public finances "more fragile" as Healey had reduced the "headroom" or the buffer that the country has between what it takes in revenues and what it spends.
Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey said the £100 energy payment would be identified as the best item in the Budget for many people, but said that it was "not good enough" when you considered the "stealth tax rises" that were taking money out of people's pay packets.

items.title: Audio reveals exchanges between Spain train operators and drivers moments before deadly crash
items.description: The leaked tapes appear to show one high-speed train was given clearance to move at normal speed, even though another up ahead had stalled.
items.content:
Audio reveals exchanges between Spain train operators and drivers moments before deadly crash
- Published
Leaked audio recordings that were published in Spanish media have revealed conversations between train drivers and a control centre just minutes before a deadly crash on Wednesday morning, that has killed 69 people.
Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train near Urda.
Three audio recordings between Madrid's control centre and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another train had stalled on the track, about 25km (15 miles) ahead.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said that authorities will "get to the bottom of every last detail of this tragedy".
Dozens of people were injured, with survivors recounting harrowing scenes people crying and bleeding, passengers trapped in their seats, missing limbs and smoke billowing throughout the carriages, one of which caught fire.
On Thursday, Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited some of the injured passengers in a hospital in Toledo.
He later expressed condolences to the victims' relatives, pledging that the investigation would determine why the crash happened, and what measures would be taken for this not to happen again.
The crash is one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history, and Spain's worst crash since 2013. On Thursday, the country began three days of national mourning.
The moving train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. The stationary train was run by private operator Iryo, and carrying 147 passengers.
A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.
But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.
The audio recordings were published by several Spanish news outlets including El Pais and RTVE.
In one, a control centre operator is speaking to the driver of the Renfe train, which was having some technical difficulties.
After some exchanges, the control operator tells the driver: "Continue your journey and then proceed under [Lateral Signalling Block], at normal speed with normal operation."
The driver replies: "At normal speed?" To which the controller answers: "Yes."
The Lateral Signalling Block is a back-up or alternative train system used when the automatic signalling or data transmission system fails.
The driver of the stationary Iryo train says in another audio recording that communication with the train-control system has been lost, and it is not moving.
The train "is stationary in front of the entry signal at Urda", the driver tells the control centre operator. After a series of exchanges, the driver is then told to "resume the journey" normally.
The Iryo driver then contacts the control centre again, according to a later recording, saying they cannot start the train. "The train won't allow me to control the [security] system. That's why I am still stopped in front of the entry signal," they say.
The latter recording suggests that the controller had been notified that the Iryo train remained stationary as the Renfe train approached.
Iryo said its carriages were "struck from behind" by the other train.
Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente said on Wednesday that the decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions, was "inexplicable".
The leaking of the audio recordings has been criticised by some Spanish politicians, with Alberto Ibáñez, a member of Congress for the left-wing Sumar platform, writing on X that they were "despicable".
Irene Montero - the prime ministerial candidate for the left-wing Podemos party - said responsibility for the crash should not be placed on one worker, adding that train drivers and experts have been warning against the liberalisation of the railway sector for years.
From the crash site, Sánchez said: "We are working day and night not only to support the victims' families, but also to establish every last detail of this tragedy and strengthen safety measures to ensure it never happens again."
Most Spanish politicians have cancelled all public engagements and suspended their campaigning ahead of a snap election on 29 November.
The exception is the far-right party Vox. Its leader, Santiago Abascal, said his party would not take part in what he described as attempts to "use mourning to silence criticism" of the country's rail infrastructure.
Overnight, around 1,500 people gathered outside the Spanish transport ministry building in the capital, according to broadcaster TVE, which reported that demonstrators were largely calling for the resignations of Sánchez and Puente.
Police used tear gas to disperse crowds after protesters hurled bottles and flares. No injuries or arrests were reported.
Rail drivers went ahead with a planned strike on Thursday, with the Spanish Union of Railway Drivers (Semaf) saying the strike action was being held "in defence of railway safety".
The leader of Spain's main opposition People's Party Alberto Núñez Feijóo said: "Spain has the right to know what is happening with its infrastructure."
At the crash site, emergency crews worked through the night under powerful floodlights to cut open metal carriages in the search for victims, with many of those killed in the crash still to be identified.
Hundreds of personnel have been deployed to the disaster site to assist with recovery efforts, Spain's interior ministry said, with drones and helicopters being used to find victims and remove rubble.
A spokesperson for the Spanish Civil Guard told the BBC they had deployed more than 900 people from different specialist departments, and the priority now was identifying the deceased.
They said they did not know how long this would take, but urged those with missing family members to go to one of the local centres which have been set up to offer DNA samples.

items.title: Met refers itself to police watchdog over letter about Meghan's father
items.description: The police force faces scrutiny over its handling of a letter containing allegations about Meghan's father.
items.content:
Met refers itself to police watchdog over letter about Meghan's father
- Published
The Metropolitan Police has referred itself to the police complaints watchdog over its handling of a letter with allegations against Thomas Markle, which was handed to his daughter, the Duchess of Sussex, in 2019.
The letter, written by Markle's first wife Roslyn Loveless, is believed to have contained claims about Meghan's father.
Markle has strongly denied recent allegations that he had possessed images of child abuse, describing them as "sick lies".
The force said it had voluntarily referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) "in respect of the decision not to inform other law enforcement agencies, and the decision to pass the letter to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex."
The Met added it intended to make further referrals to "relevant overseas law enforcement agencies", a process which it expected to be completed "in the coming days".
The letter that will be considered by the IOPC was sent to the Met's royal protection team by Roslyn Loveless, who divorced Thomas Markle in 1975 and died in 2024.
The handwritten letter was then passed to Meghan in January 2019, with the duchess saying last week that it had "made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father".
Meghan did not provide any details but said it had given her sufficient reason for not visiting Thomas Markle and not allowing him to meet his grandchildren, Archie and Lilibet.
Scotland Yard said the letter contained claims about offending outside the UK and that it had been forwarded to "the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex for their awareness".
Confirming that it had referred itself to the IPOC, the Metropolitan Police said it was aware of media reports that it had try to obtain a copy of the letter.
"While the letter did not actually contain any information specifically related to security matters, it did contain a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom," it said.
It added that the Met has carried out an initial review in recent days which has led to the voluntary referral to IOPC.
The watchdog will consider why the Met did not share the contents of the letter with other law enforcement agencies, in the UK or overseas, it contained claims of alleged offences.
There are also reports that the Met did not keep a copy of the letter and had to get a copy from the Sussexes.
Meghan, in a statement last week, said she believed the allegations in the letter "were being investigated".
But the watchdog will have to consider what happened to the warnings.
There are also likely to be questions about what royal officials knew about the letter, which was sent when Meghan was still a working royal, and which was forwarded to the Sussexes' office rather than to her personally.
Jim Gamble, former head of the Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre, previously told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that he would have expected the police to have shared any warnings.
"If you get information that comes to you about someone from a foreign jurisdiction who represents a threat to children, there's a well-worn path and generally you'd expect a UK police force to share that information," said Gamble.
"I would have expected the Metropolitan Police to have gone to the FBI to say, 'Look, this isn't proven, it's an allegation, you might want to look at it'.
Noel Rasmussen, Thomas Markle's granddaughter and niece of the Duchess of Sussex, told the BBC she was "deeply troubled by the questions surrounding the Metropolitan Police's handling of the information it received".
"If allegations of this seriousness were brought to the attention of authorities, it is reasonable to ask what steps were taken, why the information was not shared with other law enforcement agencies," she said.
"I believe those questions deserve clear, transparent answers."
Reports of the Met's handline of the letter emerged as Thomas Markle's son had told the police in the Philippines about material which was alleged to contain sexual images of children, which he had claimed to have found in possessions belonging to Meghan's father.
Thomas Markle had been in the Philippines in December 2025, undergoing hospital treatment, when Meghan wrote to him to end all contact.
Authorities in the Philippines have begun investigating the claims.
Philippine Police have obtained a warrant to examine devices seized from Markle's former home.
Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old videotapes, were handed to police by Meghan's half-brother, Thomas Markle Jr, last week.
However, officers in Cebu needed a court warrant before they could examine the items.
Thomas Markle Sr has strongly denied all the allegations against him. He has been backed by his daughter Samantha who has dismissed the claims against her father as "fake".

items.title: Jury shown CCTV of Huntingdon train staff using frying pan in defence
items.description: A train crew member shows "sheer courage and bravery in seeking to save lives", a court hears.
items.content:
CCTV shows frying pan used to stop train attacker
- Published
CCTV footage of a crew member using a frying pan to fend off a knifeman aboard a train has been shown in court.
Prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC said Samir Zitouni showed "sheer courage and bravery in seeking to save lives and defend others", during the mass stabbing on the Doncaster to London King's Cross train.
Jurors at Cambridge Crown Court saw footage of Zitouni using the pan against Anthony Williams, before the train made an unscheduled stop at Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, on 1 November 2025.
Williams, 33, of Langford Road, Peterborough, denies attempting to murder 10 people aboard the train, three people in Peterborough the day before and a boy at a London railway station.
The trial has been told that whether Williams carried out the attacks was not in question, but jurors must consider whether he intended to kill those individuals.
On the second day of the trial, Paxton told jurors the attack on Zitouni was "prolonged, persistent and brutal".
Zitouni was said to have told the defendant: "We love you, we can help you."
Other CCTV footage played in court showed people fleeing the train.
Zitouni, in what Paxton called a "blood-soaked shirt", appeared "to be one of the last off the train", and Paxton said he fell "between, essentially, the gap between the train and the platform".
The court heard both of Zitouni's lungs had been punctured and he needed four blood transfusions, chest drains and the assistance of a ventilator.
Paxton earlier said one of the passengers, Raza Aslam, had grabbed a frying pan, but was stabbed in the hand by Williams.
He said Zitouni started throwing things at the defendant and "saved" Aslam's life.
Jurors also heard that Aslam told police Williams "had the greatest delight on his face".
Aslam said: "I saw his eyes expand with pleasure. I saw the contempt on his face, like a person who's high.
"He was just loving every single moment. He loved seeing us in desperation."
Paxton also told the jury how there was hand-to-hand fighting on the train.
He said Sachin Balakrishnan was stabbed in the forearm and chest, which punctured a lung and was "just centimetres from his heart".
The jury heard a call Stephen Crean made to 999 from a locked toilet on the train, telling the operator he had been stabbed "all over" and left "covered in blood".
Commenting on CCTV footage, Paxton said: "You can see the panic, you can see the fear in the faces of those fleeing.
"In this storm of violence, and even when gripped by fear, many there on that train helped others and, as we will see, some stood tall, quite literally, against the defendant's violent onslaught."
Jurors also heard how Scott Green had been travelling on the train with his dog, Poppy.
Paxton said: "He thought he was going to lose his life on the train when the defendant tried to stab him for the third time.
"It seems, members of the jury, that Poppy the dog, for Mr Green at least, saved the day and sent the defendant running off.
"You will hear that in an unrelated incident the defendant had previously been bitten by a dog."
Huntingdon Train Attack: Day One
Following the trial of Anthony Williams from Peterborough who is accused of carrying out multiple stabbing attacks on a train in Cambridgeshire in 2025, and separate attacks.
During Thursday's evidence, the court was also told of an attack on 73-year-old David Presland, who had been stabbed in the back while on his hands and knees.
Presland said he had been "helped by someone he knew as Kevin" - believed to be Kevin Deely, another of those Williams is accused of attempting to murder.
Paxton told the court the events were "all over in about five minutes", adding: "In that time, 10 men are stabbed by one man, this defendant, Mr Williams."
Williams is accused of attempting to murder Aslam, Balakrishnan, Crean, Deely, Green, Presland and Zitouni on the train between Peterborough and Huntingdon on the Saturday evening, along with Scott Bletcher, Jonathan Gjoshe and Michael Paffett.
He is also accused of attempting to murder a 14-year-old boy and Dawid Taborski on a footbridge near Henry Penn Walk in Peterborough on 31 October, and William Ogelby at Railworld car park in the city shortly afterwards.
The trial continues.

Watch Trump arrive in New York for his arraignment

What we covered here
Former President Donald Trump arrived in New York City Monday, a day before he is expected to turn himself in to law enforcement and face more than 30 criminal charges in a Manhattan court following last week’s historic grand jury indictment.
Trump’s legal team said the former president will voluntarily surrender and will look to challenge “every potential issue” once the indictment is unsealed.
Trump, who has vowed to continue his 2024 bid, is the first current or former president in US history who has faced criminal charges. The district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential election.
Trump arraignment has "unparalleled public interest," but it won't be broadcast, judge says
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan wrote his Monday night order that the media’s request to broadcast the arraignment of former President Donald Trump was understandable, but that the news organizations’ interests in providing the broadest possible access to the proceedings must be weighed against “competing interests.”
In rejecting the request to broadcast the arraignment live on television, Merchan still wrote about the historical significance of the proceeding in stark terms.

Judge will only briefly allow photos in the courtroom before Trump arraignment begins
From CNN's Tierney Sneed
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.
Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.
However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”
Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.
The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”
The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.
The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.
Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

Tuesday is the first test for Trump to navigate a legal and political strategy
From CNN's Jeff Zeleny
Donald Trump is not planning to speak publicly in New York on Tuesday, aides say, if he follows advice from members of his legal team who have urged the former President to refrain from the vitriol he’s been directing toward the prosecutor and judge presiding over the case.
But that restraint does not extend to Florida, aides said, where he is planning to deliver a full-throated defense of his New York case as well as other investigations he is facing during a prime time address from Mar-a-Lago on Tuesday night.
It’s the first test to see whether Trump can navigate two vasty different approaches to his legal case and his political campaign, which are now inextricably linked.

Trump is "ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow," attorney says
From CNN's Mary Kay Mallonee
Alina Habba, lawyer for former President Donald Trump, gives an interview outside of Trump Tower on March 21 in New York City.
(Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Alina Habba, who represents Donald Trump in several civil matters, spent time with the former president in New York today and said, “He’s in good spirits. Honestly, he’s as he normally would be. He’s ready to go in and do what he needs to do tomorrow.”
Habba — appearing on on Fox News’ “Jesse Watters” — was asked about the “game plan” for Trump’s appearance in court in Manhattan Tuesday and said, “It’s all mapped out.”
She added, “Barring any surprises, I think that it should be smooth. We’re trying to coordinate and cooperate with everybody to make sure that there are no problems.”
On whether Trump can get a fair trial in Manhattan, Habba said, “No, no. I think it’s very difficult. I’d like to have faith in this state, but I’ve been practicing for him now for a couple years and gone to court in New York for a few years, and I can tell you, it’s not the same as representing anybody else.”

From left to right: Susan Necheles, Todd Blanche and Joe Tacopina.

Former President Donald Trump met with his attorneys Susan Necheles and Joe Tacopina at Trump Tower after arriving in New York City Monday, a source familiar with the meeting told CNN.
It is unclear if the newest addition to Trump’s New York legal team, Todd Blanche, attended the meeting.
Trump is expected to be arraigned Tuesday.

From CNN's Photo Desk
Former President Donald Trump has landed in New York’s La Guardia Airport ahead of his expected Tuesday arraignment in a Manhattan courthouse.
History was made Thursday when he was indicted by a New York grand jury. It’s the first time that a current or former US president has been criminally charged.
The Manhattan district attorney’s office has been investigating Trump’s alleged role in a hush money payment scheme and cover-up involving adult film star Stormy Daniels that dates to the 2016 presidential campaign.
Trump’s attorney said he plans to file “substantial” legal challenges. The former president has repeatedly denied wrongdoing in the matter and accused Democrats of targeting him politically.

Former president poised to huddle with advisers at Trump Tower
From Jeff Zeleny
A supporter of former President Donald Trump holds a "Trump Won" sign outside of Trump Tower in New York on Monday, April 3.
(Alex Kent/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
A small group of supporters chanted as former President Donald Trump arrived at his namesake tower on Monday afternoon, with a handful of people waving banners with messages like “Trump won” and “Arrest Biden.”
While Trump couldn’t see his admirers as he entered a side door on 56th Street, his arrival came with more fanfare and security than at any other time in his post presidency.
Now that he is inside the building — where he launched his presidential bid nearly eight years ago — Trump is expected to meet with lawyers and political advisers on the eve of his arraignment, an aide told CNN.
Trump’s mood was described by an adviser as “defiant and focused,” as he watched expansive television coverage while flying back to his native New York City from Florida.

Special counsel has secured evidence of how Trump handled classified records at Mar-a-Lago, sources say
From CNN's Katelyn Polantz and Evan Perez
Special counsel prosecutors have secured evidence including daily notes, texts, emails and photographs and are focused on cataloging how Donald Trump handled classified records around the Mar-a-Lago resort and those who may have witnessed the former president with them, according to multiple sources familiar with the investigation.
The new details come amid signs the Justice Department is taking steps that are typically near the end of an investigation.
The recent investigative activity before a federal grand jury in Washington, DC, also includes subpoenaing witnesses in March and April who had previously spoken to investigators, the sources said. While the FBI interviewed many aides and workers at Mar-a-Lago nearly a year ago voluntarily, grand jury appearances are transcribed and under oath — an indication the prosecutors are locking in witness testimony.
The focus of both the mishandling of records and obstruction of justice probes has remained on the actions of the former president, the sources say. That includes prosecutors pursuing evidence of Trump’s intent to keep classified records after he left the White House, plus his knowledge that the records remained in his possession after the Justice Department demanded their return last May.
Witnesses are being questioned about what they saw in Trump’s private residential and work areas within the club, some of the sources said.
